data.title: Stryker (SYK) President Sold Shares. How Much Do They Still Hold?
data.description:
• Group President of Global Quality & Operations Viju Menon sold $2.0m of Stryker (NYSE:SYK) stock on November 25, 2026.
  • The $2.0m disposal reduced their holding by 34%.
  • Over the last twelve months, five insiders sold shares in open market trades worth $578.6m.

Stryker insiders have been reducing exposure through open market sales. When looking for the opposite signal, where executives and directors are increasing personal financial commitment to their own businesses, it can be useful to see 69 undervalued small caps that insiders are buying.

One director dominates Stryker insider selling

Viju Menon cut exposure after a year in which their filings show only one open-market sale and one option or award exercise, so the latest move reads as a continuation rather than a change in approach for this Stryker executive.

The heavier activity came from Independent Director Ronda Stryker, whose February 2026 sale of $181.7m followed full-year results and was part of a run of disposals that in total trimmed their holding by 3%. In the three months after that trade, the company reported first quarter earnings and launched its SmartHospital Platform. By late spring the shares were 19% lower than on the day of the sale, with Ronda Stryker returning to sell again in May.

Across these filings, the shares now trade close to the average sale prices for most of the insiders. The sale by M. Fink came at a level that was 17% below where the shares change hands today, a rise they missed on the stock they sold. Taken together, the past year reads as steady selling, concentrated in one director but shared across several managers, which leans more toward caution than confidence in the way Stryker insiders handle their own holdings.

Mako execution and hospital spending have to carry Stryker

For Stryker to make these insider sales look early, the business needs its robotics push and hospital capital cycle to keep doing the heavy lifting that underpins the Narrative. On October 29, 2026, the third quarter update showed higher sales than the prior year and a different profit mix, with the share price now close to where insiders were selling.

  • Mako needs wider use, more installations and broader procedures that pull through implants and recurring service income.
  • Hospital capital budgets need to keep supporting orders for Mako systems, beds and Smart Care equipment.
  • Peripheral vascular needs to rebuild volumes as manufacturing issues clear and new thrombectomy products gain traction.

Want to know if the smart money is right to cash in? Uncover how Stryker's fair value is worked out.

Heavy insider holdings reshape what these trades mean

Several insiders sold on the open market, and the register shows that together they still own 9.3% of Stryker, a stake worth $11.5b, which is high for a company this size. Every trade comes from people whose own wealth moves with the stock. Independent Director Ronda Stryker, who traded earlier this year, is also the sixth-largest holder with 3.7% of the company, so each sale adjusts a significant personal position. John Brown is the third-largest holder with 5.3% of the company, and beside stakes this size, insider sales over the year barely change who controls the shares.

Insiders and major holders together make these trades read as portfolio moves inside a tightly held stock rather than shifts in who owns it.

For the purposes of this article, insiders are those individuals who report their transactions to the relevant regulatory body. We count open-market transactions and private dispositions of directly held shares only, not derivative transactions such as option exercises or interests held indirectly, for example through a family trust or company.

data.title: Several Insiders Invested In Neurotech International Flagging Positive News
data.description:
When a single insider purchases stock, it is typically not a major deal. However, when multiple insiders purchase stock, like in Neurotech International Limited's (ASX:NTI) instance, it's good news for shareholders.

While insider transactions are not the most important thing when it comes to long-term investing, logic dictates you should pay some attention to whether insiders are buying or selling shares.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Neurotech International

Non-Executive Director Andrew Chapman previously made an even bigger purchase of AU$301k worth of shares at a price of AU$0.014 per share. So it's clear an insider wanted to buy, at around the current price, which is AU$0.014. Of course they may have changed their mind. But this suggests they are optimistic. We do always like to see insider buying, but it is worth noting if those purchases were made at well below today's share price, as the discount to value may have narrowed with the rising price. In this case we're pleased to report that the insider purchases were made at close to current prices.

In the last twelve months Neurotech International insiders were buying shares, but not selling. The chart below shows insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year. If you want to know exactly who sold, for how much, and when, simply click on the graph below!

Insiders At Neurotech International Have Bought Stock Recently

It's good to see that Neurotech International insiders have made notable investments in the company's shares. In total, insiders bought AU$400k worth of shares in that time, and we didn't record any sales whatsoever. That shows some optimism about the company's future.

Insider Ownership

For a common shareholder, it is worth checking how many shares are held by company insiders. We usually like to see fairly high levels of insider ownership. Our data indicates that Neurotech International insiders own about AU$2.5m worth of shares (which is 11% of the company). We do note, however, it is possible insiders have an indirect interest through a private company or other corporate structure. Whilst better than nothing, we're not overly impressed by these holdings.

What Might The Insider Transactions At Neurotech International Tell Us?

It's certainly positive to see the recent insider purchases. And the longer term insider transactions also give us confidence. But we don't feel the same about the fact the company is making losses. On this analysis the only slight negative we see is the fairly low (overall) insider ownership; their transactions suggest that they are quite positive on Neurotech International stock. So while it's helpful to know what insiders are doing in terms of buying or selling, it's also helpful to know the risks that a particular company is facing. data.title: Insider Buyers Lose Additional AU$113k As Venari Minerals Dips To AU$15m
data.description:
The recent 12% drop in Venari Minerals NL's (ASX:VMS) stock could come as a blow to insiders who purchased AU$228.2k worth of stock at an average buy price of AU$0.17 over the past 12 months. This is not good as insiders invest based on expectations that their money will appreciate over time. However, as a result of recent losses, their original investment is now worth only AU$114.9k.

While we would never suggest that investors should base their decisions solely on what the directors of a company have been doing, logic dictates you should pay some attention to whether insiders are buying or selling shares.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Venari Minerals

In the last twelve months, the biggest single purchase by an insider was when Executive Chairman Anthony Leibowitz bought AU$100k worth of shares at a price of AU$0.16 per share. So it's clear an insider wanted to buy, even at a higher price than the current share price (being AU$0.087). While their view may have changed since the purchase was made, this does at least suggest they have had confidence in the company's future. To us, it's very important to consider the price insiders pay for shares. Generally speaking, it catches our eye when insiders have purchased shares at above current prices, as it suggests they believed the shares were worth buying, even at a higher price.

While Venari Minerals insiders bought shares during the last year, they didn't sell. The average buy price was around AU$0.17. These transactions suggest that insiders have considered the current price attractive. The chart below shows insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year. Does Venari Minerals Boast High Insider Ownership?

For a common shareholder, it is worth checking how many shares are held by company insiders. Usually, the higher the insider ownership, the more likely it is that insiders will be incentivised to build the company for the long term. Insiders own 25% of Venari Minerals shares, worth about AU$3.7m. We've certainly seen higher levels of insider ownership elsewhere, but these holdings are enough to suggest alignment between insiders and the other shareholders.

So What Does This Data Suggest About Venari Minerals Insiders?

It doesn't really mean much that no insider has traded Venari Minerals shares in the last quarter. But insiders have shown more of an appetite for the stock, over the last year. Insiders own shares in Venari Minerals and we see no evidence to suggest they are worried about the future.
